q: What is the difference between a coworking space and a shared office?
a: Coworking means sharing open seats; a shared office means renting a lockable room. In practice, many places offer both — co-ba ebisu has coworking on the ground floor and private offices on the 2nd.
desc: The difference between coworking and shared offices, explained with official information from co-ba ebisu, LIFORK Otemachi, co-lab Shibuya Cast and ARCH.
secs: co-ba-ebisu
Shared seats downstairs, lockable rooms upstairs
co-ba ebisu has coworking on the ground floor and private offices on the 2nd. Downstairs, a free-address membership usable 24 hours a day costs ¥30,000 a month, and a fixed BOOTH seat ¥65,000.
Upstairs, rooms of about 31–72 m² are rented on two-year fixed-term leases. In one building, there is a way in for renting a seat and a way in for renting a room.
co-ba-ebisu
co-ba-ebisu
lifork-otemachi
13 types of room, from 4 to 30 people
LIFORK Otemachi's shared offices come in 13 room types, from rooms for 4 to rooms for 20–30. They are available 24/7, with utilities included in the rent.
Each company rents its own room; the joining fee is one month's rent and the deposit 1.1 months'. It is a clear example of a shared office, contracted by the room rather than by the seat.
lifork-otemachi
co-lab-shibuya-cast
From booths for 1–2 to rooms for 22
co-lab Shibuya Cast is a shared office for creators, with 16 booths for 1–2 people, 7 studios for 3–5, 8 ateliers for 4–12 and 4 rooms for 12–22.
Flex membership with no fixed seat starts at ¥15,000 a month, and a single desk at ¥42,000. With room sizes so finely graded, both individuals and small teams can find a fit.
co-lab-shibuya-cast
co-lab-shibuya-cast
toranomon-hills-arch
CO-WORK and SMALL OFFICE on the same floor
ARCH's CO-WORK is “a varied workspace where you can choose where to work to suit the situation”, with power and network at every seat.
SMALL OFFICE is a secure second office. The same 3,800 m² floor holds both open seats and closed rooms.
toranomon-hills-arch
toranomon-hills-arch

ctx.title: What is a shared office?
body: An office where a building is divided into rooms rented by several companies or individuals, with reception, lounges and meeting rooms shared.
Where the line with coworking falls differs by place. A space centred on shared seats is usually called coworking; one centred on lockable rooms, a shared office.

q: Are there places I can use without becoming a member?
a: Yes. Day-rate drop-in, rooms by the half-hour and guided tours are all ways in. Drop-in at co-ba ebisu is ¥2,000 a day, on weekdays from 10:00 to 19:00.
desc: Ways to use coworking without membership, from the official information of co-ba ebisu, MIDORI.so, LIFORK Otemachi and 100BANCH.
secs: co-ba-ebisu
Sit down for a day for ¥2,000
Drop-in at co-ba ebisu is ¥2,000 a day, on weekdays from 10:00 to 19:00. Even non-members can try a day first.
The ground-floor coworking has Wi-Fi, power and phone booths — a way to get the feel of the place before signing a monthly contract.
co-ba-ebisu
midori-so-nakameguro
Pop-in at ¥3,300 a day, or ¥33,000 for 11 days
Pop-in at MIDORI.so Nakameguro costs ¥3,300 a day. An 11-day pack is ¥33,000, which suits people who come two or three days a week.
The main building's gallery is also rented out for exhibitions and shoots, so people other than members find their way in.
midori-so-nakameguro
lifork-otemachi
Style rooms by the half-hour
LIFORK Otemachi has ten Style Rooms, B to L: a room for 4 costs ¥1,650 per 30 minutes, and G, for 16, ¥4,400 per 30 minutes.
They are available 9:00–21:00, from a minimum of 30 minutes and then in 15-minute steps — a way to rent a room without membership.
lifork-otemachi
100banch
A 40-minute tour from 17:00 on weekdays
100BANCH runs a facility tour of about 40 minutes from 17:00 on weekdays, for ¥2,200 per person including a book.
With a way to see inside without membership, it is a good way to get a feel for a coworking space while you are looking.
100banch

ctx.title: What is drop-in?
body: Using a coworking space for a day or a few hours without a monthly contract. Some places use other names, such as “pop-in”.
Prices of around ¥2,000–3,300 a day are typical. Before joining, you can check for yourself how busy and how noisy it gets.

q: Are there coworking spaces open 24 hours?
a: Yes. co-lab Shibuya Cast, LIFORK Otemachi, MIDORI.so Nakameguro and co-ba ebisu's ground floor are open 24/7. Late-night and holiday access relies on keyless systems such as smart locks.
desc: 24-hour coworking, from the official information of co-lab Shibuya Cast, LIFORK Otemachi, MIDORI.so and co-ba ebisu.
secs: co-lab-shibuya-cast
A 24/7 shared office, running since 2003
co-lab Shibuya Cast is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year — every room alike, from booths for 1–2 to rooms for 12–22.
The 2nd floor has a window-side shared space and a kitchen, so there is somewhere to take a break outside your room, day or night.
co-lab-shibuya-cast
lifork-otemachi
A smart lock for access when reception is closed
LIFORK Otemachi's shared offices are open 24/7 (except building closure days). Members enter and leave with a smart lock.
With no key to carry, you can come and go late at night or on holidays by yourself.
lifork-otemachi
lifork-otemachi
midori-so-nakameguro
An old building, open 24/7
MIDORI.so Nakameguro is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, with a kitchen, lockers and free drinks.
Free desks cost ¥42,350 a month and fixed desks ¥60,500. With no time limits, you choose your contract by seat type.
midori-so-nakameguro
co-ba-ebisu
A 24-hour plan, and a nights-and-weekends plan
On co-ba ebisu's ground floor, a free-address membership usable 24 hours every day is ¥30,000 a month.
Night & Weekend, for weekday evenings and weekends only, is ¥12,000 a month, and Early Bird ¥6,500 — the price changes with the hours you use.
co-ba-ebisu

ctx.title: What is a smart lock?
body: An electronic lock opened with a smartphone or card instead of a physical key. LIFORK Otemachi uses one for member access.
For 24-hour spaces, managing access when no one is at reception is the key issue. Not having to hand out keys greatly reduces the work of running the place.

q: What does a community manager do?
a: They are staff who connect members with each other and with outsiders, and act as the contact point for events and advice. Their role differs from a reception desk that manages seats. At Business Airport, they are described as partners who work alongside members.
desc: What community managers do, from the official information of Business Airport Aoyama, ARCH and SHIBUYA QWS.
secs: business-airport-aoyama
Community managers who work alongside members
At Business Airport Aoyama, community managers work alongside members. Staff are on hand during reception hours, and security is in place.
Members of any site can use the coworking at every site. Whether there is someone whose job is introducing people changes how a shared office feels.
business-airport-aoyama
toranomon-hills-arch
Chief Incubation Officers who advise and connect
At ARCH, two Chief Incubation Officers give advice and connect people. The title differs, but the role is close to a community manager's.
Mentoring, networking and training are the pillars of the service, with weekly mixers, round-table gatherings and pitch events held inside.
toranomon-hills-arch
shibuya-qws
QWS Commons, who support members as experts
SHIBUYA QWS has a membership category, QWS Commons, for experts who support members. They share the floor with project members, who join in teams of three or more.
CROSS PARK, at the centre of the facility, is where people cross paths — the shape of the space itself helps connect people, not only the staff.
shibuya-qws

ctx.title: What is a community manager?
body: Staff at a coworking space or shared office who connect members with each other and with outsiders. They also plan events and act as a contact point for advice.
Titles vary. More and more places appoint people whose job is advice and introductions, like ARCH's Chief Incubation Officers.

q: How do meeting rooms and event spaces work?
a: Meeting rooms are usually booked by the hour, while event spaces are normally shared areas hired out exclusively for events. WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square has 70 meeting rooms, so you can choose the size you need.
desc: How meeting rooms and event spaces work, from the official information of WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square, LIFORK Otemachi, co-ba ebisu and SHIBUYA QWS.
secs: wework-shibuya-scramble-square
70 meeting rooms and a lounge rearranged for events
WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square has 70 meeting rooms, from small discussion rooms to larger meeting rooms.
The 42nd-floor lounge can be rearranged for events, and phone booths let you take online meetings away from your seat.
wework-shibuya-scramble-square
wework-shibuya-scramble-square
lifork-otemachi
A 199.1 m² rental lounge for ¥44,000 an hour
LIFORK Otemachi's rental lounge is 199.1 m², holding 50 seated or 60 standing, with a 130-inch screen and wireless microphones.
It costs ¥44,000 per 60 minutes, minimum 60 minutes then 15-minute steps, and is used for seminars, mixers, award ceremonies, shoots and screenings.
lifork-otemachi
lifork-otemachi
co-ba-ebisu
PARK for 70 and CAFE for 40, half price for members
co-ba ebisu's ground floor has two event spaces, PARK and CAFE. PARK holds up to 70 and CAFE up to 40, and members rent them at half price.
They are shared areas day to day, hired out only for events — work and networking on the same floor.
co-ba-ebisu
co-ba-ebisu
shibuya-qws
A 200-person hall and three meeting rooms for all members
SHIBUYA QWS's SCRAMBLE HALL is an event space for about 200, looking down on the Scramble Crossing, with three screens, sound, lighting and a green room.
Besides three meeting rooms open to all members, there are bookable private rooms.
shibuya-qws

ctx.title: What is an event space?
body: A large space for seminars, mixers and presentations. At coworking spaces, lounges and shared areas are often hired out exclusively for events.
Capacity, screens and sound, member discounts and hourly rates are the points to compare.

q: Who chooses private rooms and fixed desks?
a: People who want the space as their company's base — for company registration, a lockable room or a desk where they can leave their things. A fixed desk at MIDORI.so Nakameguro is ¥60,500 a month.
desc: Why people choose private rooms and fixed desks, from the official information of co-ba ebisu, ARCH and MIDORI.so.
secs: co-ba-ebisu
Rooms for 8 to 20 on two-year fixed-term leases
co-ba ebisu's 2nd floor is for private offices. Single and twin rooms of about 31–34 m² hold about 8 people, and suites of about 48–72 m² hold 10–20.
Leases are two-year fixed-term, including management fees. 2nd-floor tenants can add the ground-floor coworking for ¥30,000 a month.
co-ba-ebisu
co-ba-ebisu
toranomon-hills-arch
A secure second office, and short-term rooms
ARCH's SMALL OFFICE is a secure second office, also suited to new businesses run jointly by several companies.
PROJECT ROOM is a room for small teams that can be used for short projects — rented only for the period of intensive work.
toranomon-hills-arch
toranomon-hills-arch
midori-so-nakameguro
Free desks at ¥42,350 and fixed desks at ¥60,500 a month
At MIDORI.so Nakameguro, free desks cost ¥42,350 a month and fixed desks ¥60,500, both with an ¥11,000 joining fee.
The second building holds private offices, so members move between the shared areas of the main building and closed rooms on the same site.
midori-so-nakameguro

ctx.title: What is company registration?
body: Recording a company's address in the public register. Some coworking spaces let you use their address for registration with a fixed-desk or private-room contract.
Many places do not allow registration on free-desk plans, so people who need a company address choose a fixed desk or private room.

q: Where are coworking spaces linked directly to a station?
a: There is LIFORK Otemachi, linked to Otemachi Station, and WeWork and SHIBUYA QWS in Shibuya Scramble Square, linked to Shibuya Station. LIFORK Otemachi connects directly to Exits C8, C11 and C12 of Otemachi Station, and is five minutes on foot from JR Tokyo Station.
desc: Station-linked coworking, from the official information of LIFORK Otemachi, WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square, SHIBUYA QWS and Business Airport Aoyama.
secs: lifork-otemachi
Linked to Exits C8, C11 and C12 of Otemachi Station
LIFORK Otemachi is on the 1st and 2nd floors of Otemachi First Square West Tower, linked via Exits C8, C11 and C12 to Otemachi Station on the Tozai, Marunouchi, Chiyoda, Hanzomon and Toei Mita lines.
It is also five minutes on foot from the Marunouchi North Exit of JR Tokyo Station — a base focused on an environment for concentrated work.
lifork-otemachi
wework-shibuya-scramble-square
High floors linked to Shibuya Station, with five railways
WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square occupies floors 37–42 and 45 of the East Tower of Shibuya Scramble Square, linked directly to Shibuya Station.
The station is served by the JR Yamanote Line, Tokyu Toyoko and Den-en-toshi lines, Tokyo Metro Hanzomon and Fukutoshin lines, and Keio Inokashira Line.
wework-shibuya-scramble-square
wework-shibuya-scramble-square
shibuya-qws
The 15th floor of the same Shibuya Scramble Square
SHIBUYA QWS is on the 15th floor of the East Tower of Shibuya Scramble Square. Its floor of about 2,600 m² holds PROJECT BASE and the 200-person SCRAMBLE HALL.
Hours are 9:00–22:00 (last entry 21:30). Above the station, one building holds two coworking spaces: WeWork and QWS.
shibuya-qws
business-airport-aoyama
Not linked, but three minutes from Gaienmae
Business Airport Aoyama is a three-minute walk from Exit 1a of Gaienmae Station on the Ginza Line, on the 4th and 6th floors of the Spline Aoyama Tokyu Building.
The coworking is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays, so you can spend the hour before work in Aoyama.
business-airport-aoyama

ctx.title: What does “linked directly to the station” mean?
body: You can walk from the station gates or underground passages into the building without going outside — a real difference on rainy days or with luggage.
Many spaces that are not linked are still only 3–5 minutes from the station. Weigh how often you will go and what the walk from the station is like.

q: Are there coworking spaces in old buildings?
a: Yes. MIDORI.so Nakameguro is two shared-office buildings made from an ivy-covered derelict house. Because the old structure was kept as it was renovated, it has textures and shadows that new buildings lack.
desc: Coworking in renovated old buildings, centred on MIDORI.so Nakameguro and contrasted with co-ba ebisu and co-lab Shibuya Cast.
secs: midori-so-nakameguro
An ivy-covered ruin turned into a main building and an annex

MIDORI.so Nakameguro was created by renovating an ivy-covered derelict house. The main building's 3rd floor holds the workspace, lounge, meeting rooms and gallery, and the annex holds private offices.
Because the old structure was kept, it has textures and shadows new buildings lack. It is open 24/7.
midori-so-nakameguro
midori-so-nakameguro
co-ba-ebisu
By contrast, a new building opened in November 2019
co-ba ebisu opened in November 2019 on the 1st and 2nd floors of JP noie Ebisu-Nishi, with 1,573.42 m² over two floors and high-ceilinged shared areas.
Its design theme is “WORK ASSEMBLE”. In a new building, the interior theme is what gives a place its character.
co-ba-ebisu
co-lab-shibuya-cast
On the lower floors of a 17-storey building
co-lab Shibuya Cast occupies the 1st and 2nd floors of Shibuya Cast, a 17-storey building designed around the idea of “harmony in diversity”.
Next door is the café Are, loosely linking inside and outside. More than whether a building is old or new, how it meets the street shapes the impression of a place.
co-lab-shibuya-cast

ctx.title: What is renovation?
body: Keeping an old building's structure while redoing its interior and services. MIDORI.so Nakameguro renovated an ivy-covered derelict house this way.
Because it keeps character a new build cannot have, coworking is one of the strongest uses for people who own old buildings.

q: Which coworking spaces have private rooms for focused solo work?
a: Some places line up rooms for one. H¹T Ikebukuro East Exit THE GARDEN and H¹T Shinjuku West Exit each have 18 single rooms, and SENQ Meguro has 26 solo booths.
desc: Coworking with private rooms for focused solo work, from the official information of H¹T, WORK STYLING Shinagawa and SENQ Meguro.
secs: h1t-ikebukuro-higashiguchi-the-garden
18 rooms for one person
H¹T Ikebukuro East Exit THE GARDEN is on the 10th floor of the Ikebukuro Ito Building, with 18 single rooms and meeting rooms for 4 and 6.
It is open 7:00–22:30 on weekdays, weekends and holidays.
h1t-ikebukuro-higashiguchi-the-garden
h1t-shinjuku-nishiguchi
18 private rooms, boxes and 7 meeting rooms
H¹T Shinjuku West Exit is a 9th floor with 18 single rooms, boxes and 7 meeting rooms, plus an open space for 17.
It is open 7:00–22:00 every day.
h1t-shinjuku-nishiguchi
workstyling-shinagawa
“A nest for working, built for the best solo work”
WORK STYLING Shinagawa's concept is “a nest for working, where you can do the finest solo work”.
It is on the 5th and 6th floors of NBF Shinagawa Tower, linked to JR Shinagawa Station by a pedestrian deck.
workstyling-shinagawa
senq-meguro
26 solo booths and a home-like lounge
SENQ Meguro is an 8th-floor space with 26 solo booths and 13 rooms. Its concept is “working while living”.
The coworking is open 9:00–22:00 on weekdays, and the rooms 24 hours.
senq-meguro

q: Which coworking spaces are open at weekends?
a: Some keep the same hours at weekends as on weekdays. WORK STYLING Yaesu South Exit and WORK STYLING Ginza are open 8:00–22:00 at weekends too, and MIDORI.so Kichijoji 8:00–23:00 every day.
desc: Coworking open at weekends, from the official information of WORK STYLING, H¹T and MIDORI.so Kichijoji.
secs: workstyling-yaesu-minamiguchi
8:00 to 22:00 at weekends too
WORK STYLING Yaesu South Exit is on the 2nd floor of Pacific Century Place Marunouchi.
It is open 8:00–22:00 on weekdays and weekends, three minutes on foot from Tokyo Station.
workstyling-yaesu-minamiguchi
workstyling-ginza
One minute from Ginza Station, until 22:00 on weekends and holidays
WORK STYLING Ginza is on the 9th floor of Ginza Glasse.
It is open 8:00–22:00 on weekdays, weekends and holidays, one minute on foot from Ginza Station on the Tokyo Metro.
workstyling-ginza
h1t-shinjuku-nishiguchi
7:00 to 22:00 every day
H¹T Shinjuku West Exit is open 7:00–22:00 every day.
It is on the 9th floor of the Nishi-Shinjuku Showa Building, two minutes from the West Exit of Shinjuku Station.
h1t-shinjuku-nishiguchi
midori-so-kichijoji
The 8th floor of Kichijoji PARCO, until 23:00 every day
MIDORI.so Kichijoji is a coworking space on the 8th floor of Kichijoji PARCO.
It is open 8:00–23:00 every day, with a workspace, meeting rooms, a kitchen, a lounge and booths.
midori-so-kichijoji

q: Which coworking spaces open early in the morning?
a: Many open at 7:00. Coworking at most Business Airport sites opens at 7:00 on weekdays, H¹T Ikebukuro East Exit THE GARDEN at 7:00 every day, and drop-in at .andwork Shibuya runs 7:00–24:00.
desc: Coworking you can use early in the morning, from the official information of Business Airport, H¹T and .andwork.
secs: business-airport-kudanshita
Kudan Kaikan Terrace, from 7:00 on weekdays
Business Airport Kudanshita is on the ground floor of Kudan Kaikan Terrace, facing the greenery and water of the palace moat.
The coworking is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays, and the serviced offices 24 hours.
business-airport-kudanshita
h1t-ikebukuro-higashiguchi-the-garden
7:00 to 22:30 every day
H¹T Ikebukuro East Exit THE GARDEN is open 7:00–22:30 on weekdays, weekends and holidays.
It is three minutes on foot from the North Gate of JR Ikebukuro Station.
h1t-ikebukuro-higashiguchi-the-garden
andwork-shibuya
Drop-in from 7:00 to midnight
.andwork Shibuya turns the lobby of The Millennials Shibuya into a workplace.
Drop-in runs 7:00–24:00, and weekly and monthly members have 24-hour access. It costs ¥1,100 an hour or ¥3,300 a day.
andwork-shibuya

q: How does coworking inside a hotel work?
a: You rent the lobby or lounge by the hour or the day. .andwork Shibuya starts at ¥1,100 an hour and .andwork Azabujuban at ¥800 an hour. MIDORI.so Nihonbashi works as a workplace by day and a place to stay by night.
desc: How hotel coworking works, from the official information of .andwork and MIDORI.so Nihonbashi.
secs: andwork-shibuya
A hotel lobby that becomes a workplace for workers from around the world
.andwork Shibuya is inside The Millennials Shibuya, with a coworking area, lounge, kitchen and phone booths.
Prices are ¥1,100 an hour, ¥3,300 a day, and ¥29,000–34,000 a month.
andwork-shibuya
andwork-azabujuban
A 2nd-floor lounge and a top-floor bar
.andwork Azabujuban is inside THE LIVELY Tokyo Azabujuban, with a lounge on the 2nd floor and a bar on the top floor.
It is open 8:00–22:00, at ¥800 an hour, ¥2,500 a day or ¥34,000 a month.
andwork-azabujuban
midori-so-nihonbashi
Working and staying in the same building
MIDORI.so Nihonbashi has a café, bar and gallery on the ground floor, a lounge on the 2nd, and rooms for work and sleep on the 3rd and 4th.
Pop-in is ¥2,200 for a day or ¥8,800 for a night, with no joining or membership fee.
midori-so-nihonbashi

q: How much does coworking cost per month?
a: Plans for shared seats range from the ¥10,000s to the ¥60,000s a month. Free desks at DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO start at ¥18,700 a month, and at MIDORI.so Nakameguro cost ¥42,350.
desc: Monthly coworking prices, from the official information of MIDORI.so and DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO.
secs: midori-so-nakameguro
Free desk ¥42,350, fixed desk ¥60,500 a month
At MIDORI.so Nakameguro, a free desk is ¥42,350 a month and a fixed desk ¥60,500, with an ¥11,000 joining fee.
It is a two-building shared office made from an ivy-covered derelict house.
midori-so-nakameguro
diagonal-run-tokyo
Free desks from ¥18,700 a month
At DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO, free desks start at ¥18,700 a month. Drop-in is ¥3,300 a day, or ¥660 an hour on weekdays.
It is on the 4th floor of the Kyobashi MID Building, about a minute on foot from Takaracho Station.
diagonal-run-tokyo

q: Which coworking spaces can I use by the hour?
a: Some offer hourly drop-in. DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO is ¥660 an hour on weekdays, .andwork Azabujuban ¥800 an hour and .andwork Shibuya ¥1,100 an hour.
desc: Coworking you can use from one hour, from the official information of DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO, .andwork and MIDORI.so Nihonbashi.
secs: diagonal-run-tokyo
¥660 an hour on weekdays
DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO costs ¥660 an hour on weekdays, or ¥3,300 a day.
It describes itself as a place where people, companies and ideas from Tokyo and all over Japan cross diagonally.
diagonal-run-tokyo
andwork-azabujuban
¥800 an hour, with a 10-visit pass
.andwork Azabujuban costs ¥800 an hour or ¥2,500 a day. A 10-visit pass is ¥17,500.
It is open 8:00–22:00.
andwork-azabujuban
andwork-shibuya
¥1,100 an hour, drop-in until midnight
.andwork Shibuya costs ¥1,100 an hour or ¥3,300 a day.
Drop-in runs from 7:00 until midnight.
andwork-shibuya
midori-so-nihonbashi
Daytime pop-in at ¥2,200 a day
Daytime pop-in at MIDORI.so Nihonbashi is ¥2,200 a day, with no joining or membership fee.
At night you can stay in the same building for ¥8,800.
midori-so-nihonbashi

q: Which coworking spaces have a rooftop or terrace?
a: Some have a rooftop garden or farm, others a terrace on a high floor. SENQ Roppongi has a 9th-floor sky terrace, MIDORI.so Bakuroyokoyama a rooftop farm and THE HUB Nihonbashi Kabutocho a rooftop terrace.
desc: Coworking with a rooftop or terrace, from the official information of SENQ Roppongi, MIDORI.so and THE HUB.
secs: senq-roppongi
A 9th-floor sky terrace in Shin-Roppongi Building
SENQ Roppongi's 9th floor has about 70 coworking seats, meeting rooms, a café corner and a sky terrace.
Its theme is CHANGE THE THEORY. Private rooms are available 24/7.
senq-roppongi
midori-so-bakuroyokoyama
A farm on the roof of a Showa-era building
MIDORI.so Bakuroyokoyama fills seven floors of a Showa-era building with a café, print workshop, gallery and workspace.
On the roof is a garden used as a farm.
midori-so-bakuroyokoyama
the-hub-nihonbashi-kabutocho
Fully private rooms and a rooftop terrace
THE HUB Nihonbashi Kabutocho is a boldly renovated SOHO building. Every room is fully private, and there is a rooftop terrace.
There are three meeting rooms for 4, and private rental offices start at ¥75,350 a month.
the-hub-nihonbashi-kabutocho

q: Which coworking spaces have themed interiors?
a: Some bring local history or a story into their interiors. WORK STYLING's Hibiya site is “ZEN MODERN” and its Shinjuku Mitsui Building site “RETRO FUTURE”; Business Airport uses a theatre motif in Hibiya and the railway in Shimbashi.
desc: Coworking with themed interiors, from the official information of WORK STYLING and Business Airport.
secs: workstyling-tokyo-midtown-hibiya
“ZEN MODERN” with traditional Japanese patterns
WORK STYLING Tokyo Midtown Hibiya is on the 12th floor of Hibiya Mitsui Tower.
Its design theme is “ZEN MODERN”, decorated with traditional Japanese patterns.
workstyling-tokyo-midtown-hibiya
workstyling-shinjuku-mitsui-building
“RETRO FUTURE”, spanning past and future
WORK STYLING Shinjuku Mitsui Building is on the 11th floor. Its design theme is “RETRO FUTURE”.
FLEX members have 24-hour access.
workstyling-shinjuku-mitsui-building
business-airport-hibiya
A theatre motif, surrounded by greenery and art
Business Airport Hibiya is on the 9th floor of the Toho Hibiya Building, a workplace with a theatre motif.
The coworking is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays and 10:00–18:00 on weekends and holidays.
business-airport-hibiya
business-airport-shimbashi
Motifs recalling the birthplace of Japan's railways
Business Airport Shimbashi is on floors 6–8 of Shimbashi Place, full of motifs recalling the birthplace of Japan's railways.
There are four meeting rooms.
business-airport-shimbashi

q: Which coworking spaces are on high floors with a view?
a: Some occupy the upper floors of skyscrapers. WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square is on floors 37–42 and 45, WORK STYLING Kasumigaseki Building on the 36th, and Business Airport Shinagawa on the 28th.
desc: High-floor coworking with a view, from the official information of WeWork, WORK STYLING and Business Airport.
secs: wework-shibuya-scramble-square
Floors 37–42 and 45, linked to Shibuya Station
WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square uses floors 37–42 and 45 of a 47-storey tower.
There are 70 meeting rooms, with ceilings of 3,000–3,200 mm.
wework-shibuya-scramble-square
workstyling-kasumigaseki-building
The 36th floor of the Kasumigaseki Building
WORK STYLING Kasumigaseki Building is on the 36th floor.
It is two minutes on foot from Toranomon Station on the Ginza Line.
workstyling-kasumigaseki-building
business-airport-shinagawa
The 28th floor of the Taiyo Life Shinagawa Building
Business Airport Shinagawa is on the 28th floor of the Taiyo Life Shinagawa Building.
It has rooms for 1–6, desks, coworking and three meeting rooms.
business-airport-shinagawa

q: Which coworking spaces can host seminars or large meetings?
a: Some have large meeting rooms or event spaces. Global Business Hub Tokyo has an event space for up to 200, WORK STYLING Ebisu a conference room for up to 150, and X-NIHONBASHI TOWER about 120 seats in theatre style.
desc: Coworking for large groups, from the official information of Global Business Hub Tokyo, WORK STYLING Ebisu, X-NIHONBASHI TOWER and CROSSCOOP.
secs: global-business-hub-tokyo
An event space for up to 200
Global Business Hub Tokyo is on the 3rd floor of Otemachi Financial City Grand Cube.
It has 50 furnished offices, 14 meeting rooms and an event space for up to 200.
global-business-hub-tokyo
workstyling-ebisu
A conference room for 13 to 150
WORK STYLING Ebisu has a conference room for 13 to 150 people.
It is on the 8th floor of the Fujiwara Building, one minute on foot from Ebisu Station on the Tokyo Metro.
workstyling-ebisu
x-nihonbashi-tower
About 120 seats in theatre style
X-NIHONBASHI TOWER is a co-creation hub for the space business on the 7th floor of Nihonbashi Mitsui Tower.
At 307 m², it seats about 120 in theatre style or holds about 150 standing.
x-nihonbashi-tower
crosscoop-shimbashi
A seminar room for 72
CROSSCOOP Shimbashi has a seminar room for 72 and a lounge of about 96 seats.
Private offices are for 10 to 100 people, and shared facilities are available 24 hours.
crosscoop-shimbashi

q: How do I pay at a coworking space in Japan?
a: Most drop-in spaces take cards, and several take no cash at all. SENQ's drop-in accepts credit cards, transit IC cards, Apple Pay, iD and QUICPay but not cash, and NAKANO HAKO is cashless only.
desc: Payment methods at coworking spaces in Japan — cash, cards, transit IC cards, PayPay and apps — from the official information of SENQ, NAKANO HAKO, Noblesse Oblige, BasisPoint and Rembrally Cafe.
secs: senq-kyobashi
Cards and e-money, no cash
SENQ's drop-in, offered at Kyobashi, Kasumigaseki, Roppongi, Meguro and Aoyama Namikidori, accepts credit cards and e-money: transit IC cards, Apple Pay, iD and QUICPay.
Cash is not accepted, and cards cannot be topped up at the desk. You sign up at reception without booking; it costs ¥550 an hour plus a one-time ¥550 joining fee.
senq-kyobashi
nakano-hako
Cashless only
NAKANO HAKO takes credit cards, e-money and QR payments, and no cash.
You check in at reception and wear a user card while you are inside; private booths can be booked in the SHARE LOUNGE app.
nakano-hako
noblesse-oblige-kashiwa
Cash, card, e-money or PayPay
At Noblesse Oblige in Kashiwa you register at the staffed reception on your first visit and pay by cash, credit card, e-money or PayPay.
Drop-in is ¥660 an hour or ¥1,980 a day.
noblesse-oblige-kashiwa
basispoint-shimbashi-ginzaguchi
Pay when you leave
BasisPoint lets you register free at reception, sit anywhere in the open space and pay for the time you used when you leave.
It accepts cash, credit cards, e-money and QR payments; drop-in starts at ¥330 per 30 minutes with a daily cap.
basispoint-shimbashi-ginzaguchi
rembrally-cafe-ebina
An app, or cash at the hotel desk
Rembrally Cafe in Ebina has no staff: you unlock the door and pay in the Threes app, from ¥250 for the first 30 minutes up to ¥1,500 a day.
Visitors who prefer cash apply and pay at the front desk of the hotel next door.
rembrally-cafe-ebina

ctx.title: What is a transit IC card?
body: Suica and PASMO are the rechargeable cards used on trains and buses around Tokyo. Many shops also accept them as e-money.
SENQ lists transit IC cards among its payment methods, and at H¹T members can register one as their door key.

q: Which coworking spaces have English-speaking staff or an English website?
a: CIC Tokyo says it has bilingual staff, and StartupSide Tokyo has staff who speak English, Chinese and Malay. Operators such as The Executive Centre, JustCo and MIDORI.so publish English websites, while THE HUB states that its contracts require Japanese.
desc: English support at coworking spaces in Japan, from the official information of CIC Tokyo, StartupSide Tokyo, The Executive Centre, Thermae-Yu and THE HUB.
secs: cic-tokyo
Bilingual staff
CIC Tokyo lists bilingual staff among its services, together with 24-hour access and an English website.
It is a membership space with coworking desks and private offices; members book meeting rooms in the booking system.
cic-tokyo
startupside-tokyo
Staff who speak English, Chinese and Malay
StartupSide Tokyo has staff who speak English, Chinese and Malay, and supports companies expanding abroad or into Japan.
It is open 24 hours a day.
startupside-tokyo
the-executive-centre-jingumae-tower
A Day Pass you can book in English
The Executive Centre sells a Day Pass to first-time visitors. You book on its English website, in the MyTEC app or at reception, then check in at reception.
Day Pass access is usually during standard business hours, about 9:00–18:00.
the-executive-centre-jingumae-tower
thermae-yu-shinjuku
A hot spring with an English website
Thermae-Yu in Shinjuku publishes its website in English, Korean and Chinese, and takes cards, PayPay, Alipay and UnionPay.
Tattoos are allowed for overseas visitors only.
thermae-yu-shinjuku
the-hub-akasaka
Where Japanese is required
THE HUB states that its service is in Japanese and that contract holders need to read, write and speak Japanese.
Its drop-in, 10-hour and weekend plans are registered in the official app and paid by credit card.
the-hub-akasaka

q: What do I need for my first visit?
a: It depends on the space. Some let you walk in and sign up at reception, some ask you to register in an app before you arrive, and monthly plans usually need photo ID.
desc: What to expect on a first visit to a coworking space in Japan — walk-in, app registration, booking and ID — from the official information of MONO, RoomUs, tefu, co-ba akasaka and Business-Airport.
secs: coworking-space-mono-aomi
Walk in and sign at reception
MONO in Aomi needs no booking or registration for drop-in: you check in at reception, and on your first visit you sign the terms of use.
Drop-in runs on weekdays from 10:00 to 18:00, for 2 hours or a full day.
coworking-space-mono-aomi
roomus-yokohama
Register online before you go
RoomUs Yokohama is unstaffed, so you register online before your first visit.
It charges ¥100 per 20 minutes and is open 7:00–23:00 every day.
roomus-yokohama
tefu-lounge-shimokitazawa
Sign up in the LINE app
The (tefu) lounge is used through the LINE app: you register with a credit card, choose a plan and check in, and you can book before you arrive.
Lounge users get free specialty coffee.
tefu-lounge-shimokitazawa
co-ba-akasaka
Book first — no walk-ins
co-ba akasaka takes drop-in only through the STATION WORK booking site and does not accept same-day visitors without a booking.
A day is ¥2,200, on weekdays from 10:00 to 19:00.
co-ba-akasaka
business-airport-tokyo
Photo ID for monthly plans
Business-Airport asks for photo ID — a driving licence, passport or My Number card — when you sign up, and you can start the same day.
Its plans run for at least two months.
business-airport-tokyo
